findings.title: website_name bypasses the TL0/anonymous restriction that hides website
findings.body:
`website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is stripped when an anonymous viewer looks at a TL0 user (`scope.restrict_user_fields?`). This anti-spam measure keeps new users' links out of public profiles. The new `website_name` attribute is derived from the same value but is not in that list, so it is always serialized and reveals the host, and sometimes the full path, of the TL0 user's website.

The template now renders `model.website_name`, so the website text appears on the profile even though `website` was withheld. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`, and add it to the TL0 spec's `untrusted_attributes` list, which currently does not catch this.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the `?` suffix and is never called
findings.body:
ActiveModel::Serializers looks for `include_<attr>?` predicates. `def include_website_name` has no `?`, so the serializer never invokes it. It is dead code: `website_name` is always emitted, as `null` when there is no website.

Even renamed to `include_website_name?`, checking only `website.present?` would still skip the `restrict_user_fields?` check. The correct fix is to cover `website_name` via `untrusted_attributes` and drop this method.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic treats unrelated domains under public suffixes as the same site
findings.body:
When both hosts have the same number of labels (more than 2), the code drops the first label and compares the rest. For instance hosts like `forum.co.uk` or `forum.github.io`, any website such as `evil.co.uk` or `someone.github.io` matches. Those unrelated sites then have their full path shown as if they belonged to the forum's own domain. The comparison is also case-sensitive: `URI#host` keeps the user's casing while `current_hostname` is lowercase, so `http://Example.com/...` won't match.

This branch has no spec coverage; the three new tests only exercise the equal-host branch and the parent-domain branch.
